sessions.title: Recognize the two taught aspect pairs

steps.title: Aspect and time
steps.body: Aspect describes how an action is viewed, not when it happens. Imperfective can focus on an activity, repetition, or the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint. Perfective presents an event with its boundary or result. Imperfective does not by itself mean unfinished. говори́ть is imperfective; сказа́ть is perfective. These infinitives do not specify tense on their own.

steps.title: The saying and telling pair
steps.body: Many Russian verbs are learned in an aspect pair, but not every verb has two words, and a pair is not automatic. говорить and сказать are context-dependent counterparts, not a universal pair for the English verb speak. For the saying/telling pair shown here, the perfective counterpart of говори́ть is сказа́ть; the imperfective counterpart of сказа́ть is говори́ть. These checks ask you to recognize this vocabulary pair, not choose aspect in a sentence.

steps.title: A worked doing and making pair
steps.body: де́лать is imperfective; сде́лать is perfective. Both concern doing or making. The perfective focuses on accomplishing the action; the imperfective can describe the activity or its occurrence without that focus. Given де́лать and a request for its perfective counterpart, choose сде́лать. говори́ть concerns speaking or saying and belongs to the other pair. Learn the shown pair rather than assuming every prefix changes only aspect.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Choose the counterpart from the saying/telling pair. Then compare its aspect and meaning with the other option.

sessions.title: Choose the admitted past aspect line

steps.title: Admitted lines
steps.body: The supplied lines я читал — I was reading and я прочитал — I read are both past-tense forms with masculine singular agreement. The line я читал is imperfective past; the line я прочитал is perfective past. The first presents reading as activity or process; the second presents it as a completed whole. These English labels describe the retained examples; they are not a rule matching every English past tense to one Russian aspect.

steps.title: Admitted instruction
steps.body: Do not treat English past progressive and simple past as a fixed Russian aspect code. The imperfective does not always mean the action was unfinished. An activity may have ended and still be described imperfectively when the focus is its process or occurrence rather than its endpoint. Recognize the requested aspect in these supplied choices; this is not unrestricted sentence production.

steps.title: Admitted lines
steps.body: чита́ть is the supplied infinitive; чита́л is its masculine singular past form. The dictionary label read names the recorded meaning and does not itself distinguish English past from infinitive. Compare the entire supplied forms. A question requesting masculine past asks for чита́л rather than feminine чита́ла; both past forms belong to the same imperfective verb.

steps.title: Interpret the nationality report
steps.body: A past reporting frame can contain a statement whose tense is interpreted from the reported speaker’s perspective. Он сказа́л, что он англича́нин has a past said verb and no past copula in the nationality statement. The supplied original is “I am English”. Past reporting verb with present nationality statement. is the matching description. The source’s alternative with a past copula changes the stated reading. That alternative can be grammatical in a different context; it is not this supplied present-nationality report. This nationality context was also taught earlier, so it is not unseen evidence.

steps.title: Separate reporting time from embedded time
steps.body: Я скажу ему ве́чером is the direct statement “I will tell him in the evening”. Она́ сказа́ла, что она́ ска́жет ему́ ве́чером is the supplied reported evening context. Past reporting verb with a future embedded action. describes its two finite verbs: said is past, and the embedded telling action retains future form within reported content. This does not imply the action must still be future compared with the present moment. The source supplies these speaker/pronoun choices; do not mechanically replace every I with she or manufacture new reported clauses.

steps.title: Distinguish a report, direct statement and time clause
steps.body: Когда́ я бу́ду в Москве́, я бу́ду говори́ть то́лько по-ру́сски gives a future time clause and a plan to speak Russian. It has no past reporting frame. Existing independent choices distinguish this supplied Moscow plan and the direct evening statement. The added independent check must also interpret the evening report’s past reporting verb and future embedded action. English backshift is not compulsory in every report; preserving these source readings is not a universal rule that every tense or word stays unchanged. This small set supports recognition of supplied contexts, not unrestricted reported-speech production.
